claims: The Artemis II crew safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT).
The Orion capsule landed approximately 50 nautical miles offshore.
The Artemis II mission was a 10-day moon mission.
Recovery teams were stationed to bring the astronauts onto the USS John P. Murtha.
The landing was a splashdown of the Orion capsule.
The U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha was the recovery ship.
The Artemis II splashdown marked the end of the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
The first crewed flight of the Artemis program successfully completed a journey around the moon.
According to NBC News, the Artemis II splashdown was the first time astronauts have returned to the Pacific coast since the Apollo era.
